  "rationale": "Repair of the concrete failure recorded in inputs/previous-feedback.txt, and how it changes this attempt: the rejected bundle trial-constraint-repair-0dbfc106-param-bb7dfba4 replaced only 12 of the 13 final-backward collectives and moved them onto a freshly initialized second NCCL communicator (direct ProcessGroupNCCL construction with NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_ALGO windows and ncclConfig CTA knobs) while the 157,541,376-byte embedding-bucket allreduce stayed on the default process group. It passed quality with max_abs_error 0.0 and even lowered the discovery kernel sum (225.85 -> 139.87 ms), but clean paired AB/BA step_ms regressed from 146.88 to 240.51 ms (paired gains -89.91/-97.35 ms, noise bounds 4.30/3.80 ms) and all tuned parameter points landed at 247-252 ms, so the split-communicator mechanism itself - not the transport knob values - was the regression; the supplemental resource_tradeoff note further warns that intrusive discovery timings are not clean critical-path evidence. This attempt therefore uses the joint two-group boundary exactly as selected: both call IDs (d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 x 28,351,488-byte regular buckets; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, the 157,541,376-byte embedding bucket) are replaced by one candidate that keeps every one of the 13 collectives on the workload's single default NCCL communicator and stream, issued through the same process-group backend object the parent c10d::allreduce_ operator resolves for this device, with parent-identical in-place ReduceOp.SUM semantics on the same bucket tensors and the same async Work contract returned to the DDP reducer. No second communicator is created, no env windows are touched, no streams or graphs are introduced, and no NCCL transport settings are modified (the default communicator was initialized by the worker before build(), so honest transport retuning is out of reach and is not claimed). The single degree of freedom left is where rank-arrival skew is absorbed: target-resources.json shows the max-rank diagnostic at 192.47 ms (rank 0: 12 kernels at 13.6-16.6 ms plus the 19.5 ms tail) versus 63.44 ms on rank 1 (12 kernels at the 3.5-3.6 ms wire floor, symmetric 19.5 ms tail), i.e. roughly 129 ms of the objective is peer-wait spun inside NCCL kernels, and the waiting rank flipped between discoveries, proving session-dependent arrival skew rather than a payload property. route=parent is the exact null point (bit-identical baseline routing, the safety floor for the paired revalidation); route=align_first inserts one CPU-side barrier on the adapter's gloo control group before the first collective of each 13-call synchronization sequence (marker-based detection: the embedding-bucket call is the last collective of every run, so the call immediately after it - or the first call ever - opens each sequence on both ranks symmetrically), moving the early rank's wait from GPU time inside the stretched kernels to bounded pre-issue CPU wait so both ranks' kernels run near their observed wire floor while the late rank's timeline is untouched; route=align_each applies the same barrier before every collective for tight per-bucket pairing. The barriers are gloo, not NCCL, so the measured workload's NCCL collective inventory is unchanged and no NCCL kernel is added or removed - all 13 allreduces still execute as real collectives on every invocation. Composition: this candidate's groups are disjoint from the 21 compute groups owned by the installed quality-passing bundle trial-32cd1ce604-param-3a67a278, which stays active and untouched (requires=[], replaces=[]); both bundles execute on both ranks, and coexistence of a communication-path candidate with that compute bundle is already demonstrated by the rejected trial's passing gradient/parameter checks over the same composition. Per the composition protocol no positive gain is required to demonstrate compatibility and no slower combination will be published. All effect magnitudes above are hypotheses to be tested, not predicted guarantees: acceptance is only via the paired clean AB/BA step_ms protocol with the 1.05x step_ms gate, and the communication objective is re-collected in separate clean collector runs; if the clean-run skew proves mostly discovery-only, the align routes are compatibility-neutral and the parent route reproduces the baseline exactly.",

      "In align modes, a dist.barrier(group=state['control']) runs on the CPU before the first collective of each synchronization sequence (align_first) or before every collective (align_each); it adds no NCCL kernel and no device work.",
      "Both ranks run identical build() code with identical parameters and identical observed call sequences (12 + 1 per run per rank_specs), so routing and barrier positions are symmetric; the mapping is returned on both ranks."
    ],
    "memory": "Setup allocates only trivial Python objects (two closures and two boolean flags): no device tensors, no CUDA Graphs, no retained pools, and - unlike the rejected trial - no second NCCL communicator, so no additional NCCL driver allocations are introduced (framework.peak_allocated_bytes / peak_reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peaks are expected unchanged from the installed-bundle baseline). The declared warm-model metric is step_ms, not a memory counter, and no memory saving is claimed.",
    "timing_scope": "All setup work runs inside build(), before validation and measurement. The measured run() still executes the frozen workload: optimizer.zero_grad, four forward/backward micro-batches (first three under DDP no_sync), the 13 gradient-bucket allreduces of the final micro-step's backward on the single default NCCL communicator, one optimizer.step(), and the closing synchronize. The only added work inside the timer is the CPU-side gloo barrier of the align routes on the owned synchronization path; the framework's own control coordination stays outside the timer and is not modified."
  },
  "quality_risks": [
    "The boxed ReduceOp argument of c10d::allreduce_ is not introspectable from Python, so the replacement reconstructs AllreduceOptions with ReduceOp.SUM. This matches the frozen semantics (DDP default allreduce hook, no communication hooks in the measured path, ReduceOp.SUM recorded for every observation); a hypothetical non-SUM call would execute incorrectly and fail the source's atol=0 cross-rank check and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference checks loudly rather than silently.",
    "Barrier symmetry: alignment positions are derived from a marker (the call following the embedding-bucket call, or the first call ever), and both ranks observe identical per-run sequences (12 regular + 1 embedding on each rank), so barriers always pair. If sequences ever diverged, the control group's bounded 120 s barrier timeout would raise and fail the run loudly; the framework restores the parent on failure. No silent numeric corruption path exists.",
    "The align routes block the DDP reducer's calling thread until the peer reaches the same collective, which trades in-kernel GPU spin-wait for pre-issue CPU wait and could perturb communication/compute overlap. This is bounded by the workload's step_ms <= 1.05x baseline gate, measured by the paired AB/BA protocol; a repeat of the previous -90/-97 ms regression fails immediately, and route=parent is the exact null point reproducing baseline routing.",
    "The align routes add a gloo collective inside the timed region (outside NCCL): the measured workload's NCCL collective inventory is unchanged, outputs, gradients, parameter updates and bitwise two-rank fp32 SUM on the same default communicator are preserved, but step_ms includes the barrier cost honestly; no diagnostic-counter decrease is claimed as a physical memory or wire-byte saving.",
    "Quality/coverage: every one of the 13 collectives per run still executes as a real allreduce through the replacement (candidate call counting sees both call IDs; reference invocations occur only for non-observed signature fallbacks, which none of the observed calls use); no calls are eliminated, so no consumer-validity question arises.",
    "Environment assumptions are minimal and guarded: torch._C._distributed_c10d ProcessGroup.unbox/_get_backend are used exactly as in the previously quality-passing implementation on this torch build; a missing control group or uninitialized distributed state silently disables alignment (route degrades to the parent-identical path) rather than crashing a run."
  ],
  "eliminated_calls": [],
  "requires": [],
  "replaces": [],
  "parameter_space": {
    "params": [
      {
        "name": "route",
        "kind": "str",
        "choices": [
          "parent",
          "align_first",
          "align_each"
        ],
        "description": "parent: issue every one of the 13 bucket allreduces on the workload's default NCCL communicator through the parent's process-group backend with identical in-place SUM options (bit-identical baseline routing, exact null point). align_first: additionally run one CPU-side gloo barrier on the adapter's control group before the first collective of each per-run synchronization sequence (first call ever, or the call right after the embedding-bucket allreduce), absorbing rank-arrival skew before kernels launch instead of inside NCCL kernels. align_each: run the same barrier before every one of the 13 collectives for tight per-bucket pairing. All routes keep every collective real, on the same communicator, with the same tensors and semantics."
      }
    ],
    "constraints": []
  }
}
